title: Research Loop 01: What Can Research Agents Actually Automate?
description:
Which research tasks can students delegate to agents while retaining responsibility for the experiment? Research Loop examines author-reported protein model results, Agora’s shared experiment history, and Periodic Labs’ account of AI-assisted laboratory work.

The evidence supports bounded delegation, with human objectives and validation decisions. It does not establish fully autonomous discovery or portable speed and cost gains. The protein result is a proxy improvement; Agora’s history does not establish independent validation; Periodic’s commercially interested testimony uses a provisional transcript.

As of: 2026-10-15 UTC. Frozen evidence window: September 16–October 15, 2026. Agora’s reported execution occurred April 26–May 8, before this publication window.


Sources and locators:

- Li and Lu: NanoProteinLM: https://jojoml.github.io/blog/2026/nanoproteinlm-agenticls/ — “A better PLM recipe by hill-climbing NanoProteinLM”; “Building hill-climbable environments for research tasks”; “Failure mode: Perfect on reward, failure on science.”
- Agora: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18094 — §4.3, “Negative results,” “Primary result,” §4.7 and §4.8.
- Periodic Labs interview: https://www.latent.space/p/periodic — recording 00:50:46–00:51:39, 01:04:24–01:05:04 and 01:15:06–01:16:53. Transcript provisional.

Companion article (free): https://researchloopweibing.substack.com/p/research-loop-delegate-the-experiment

title: Research Loop 02: Why a Better Score Can Mislead You
description:
A higher search score is only one part of an experimental result. Research Loop examines four author-reported cases involving protein-model recipes, kernel validity and transfer, production metrics, and agent harness comparisons.

The practical takeaway: report implementation validity, metric improvement and progress toward the intended objective separately. Findings remain bounded by the authors’ protocols, baselines and limitations. These separate cases do not supply independent replication of a general effect.

As of: 2026-10-15 UTC. Evidence window: 2026-09-16–2026-10-15, inclusive.


Sources and text locators:

- Protein-search report: https://jojoml.github.io/blog/2026/nanoproteinlm-agenticls/ — “Failure mode: Perfect on reward, failure on science”; “What survived the human gate.”
- Kernel Autoresearch: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10394 — “Results and failure modes”; “Repeated generation and a formulation-first prompt”; Appendix B.7, “The real-data check is less favorable”; “Long-horizon diagnostic.”
- AutoResearch at Production Scale: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30541 — “III-E Metric Fixation”; “V-E Validation Protocol”; “Limitations.”
- Malena harness study: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40303 — opening excerpt beginning “We then confirm the same picture”; “D.2 Detailed MLE-bench results”; “Limitations.”

All cited materials are text sources. Locators identify sections or excerpts; there are no recording timestamps.

title: Research Loop 03: Build an Experiment Someone Else Can Check
description:
How can student researchers make agent experiments checkable? Research Loop examines instruction optimization, held-out comparisons, provenance, claim-level evaluation and resource accounting.

As of 2026-10-15 (UTC). Frozen evidence window: September 16–October 15, 2026. This is an editorial synthesis of supplied evidence, not a new live collection. Reported findings remain attributed to their authors; the proposed student protocol is interpretation, not a replication guarantee.


Sources and locators:

- AI Code King tutorial: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wMQB33rM28I: source recording timestamps 00:56.800–01:01.780; 04:30.980–04:35.980; 10:49.900–10:53.820; 11:35.580–11:47.580; 13:29.460–13:38.780.
- Campus Talks: How is AI affecting open research?: https://timeshighered.podbean.com/e/campus-talks-how-is-ai-affecting-open-research/: source recording timestamps 16:14.680–16:20.000; 39:07.310–39:10.510; 41:08.670–41:11.870; 41:13.710–41:16.430; 54:36.070–54:40.270.
- ResearchFlow-Eval: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18088: §3.3 “LLM judge”; §6; task-package “Data and test access”; Appendix G and Table 16.
- Malena paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40303: §5.1, Figure 3 cost discussion and results-table inconsistency; Appendix A.4, modeled cache costs.

Limitations: automatic transcripts remain provisional. The tutorial does not establish measured improvement; podcast guidance is not a tested intervention. ResearchFlow-Eval uses one anchor task and permits logged test access during optimization. Malena’s costs are modeled, and its supplied comparative-results inconsistency remains unresolved. These sources do not independently validate the proposed combined protocol.
